description: t.w0 (r.side) write-locks rw and sleeps; t.w1 (r.side) and then t.w2 (r.main) queue for writes (seed 42 dispatches t.w0, t.w1, t.w2 in that order at 0). r.side is cancelled at 50 and the cancel lane runs t.w0, t.x, t.w1: t.w0's sleep ends and its release hands the lock to the front writer t.w1 although t.w1 is cancel-pending (Rust pop_writer_waiter, sync/rwlock.rs:385); t.x's notify_one wakes t.n; t.w1's poll observes the cancel and gives the lock up, waking t.w2. So t.n joins the ready lane before t.w2. C used to skip cancel-pending waiters when granting and woke t.w2 at t.w0's release, ahead of t.n (dispatch 10; bd-rm2d, as bd-z783 for the mutex).
